query: Which material can be used for enhance glass-forming ability, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Minor addition of boron to a CoCrFe-based alloy will significantly increase its glass-forming ability by lowering the critical cooling rate and stabilizing the supercooled liquid region.
generation.material_initial_state: A baseline CoCrFe-based alloy in the fully molten state prior to solidification.
generation.intervention: Introduce 1–2 at% boron into the CoCrFe-based alloy via arc melting followed by homogenization.
generation.conditions: Use melt-spinning at controlled high cooling rates (on the order of 10^5–10^6 K/s) to capture the amorphous structure, varying B content from 0 to 2 at%.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced short-range atomic order that reduces nuclei formation, inhibiting crystallization during rapid cooling.
generation.mechanism: Boron additions promote a higher atomic packing density and compositional heterogeneity, delaying the onset of crystallization and extending the supercooled liquid region.
generation.predicted_outcome: Alloys with 1–2 at% B exhibit larger critical casting thickness and a broadened supercooled liquid region compared to the baseline, demonstrating improved glass-forming ability.
generation.baseline: The unmodified CoCrFe-based alloy without boron shows lower critical thickness and more rapid crystallization during cooling.
generation.boundary: Excessive B content could form borides or other crystalline phases, negating the glass-forming benefit and reducing ductility.
generation.uncertainty: It remains unknown whether similar improvements apply across different compositions or processing routes, and further tests are required.

falsification_experiment.design: Arc melt two series of alloys—(CoCrFe)100–xBx with x=0 and 1–2 at%. Perform melt-spinning at identical cooling rates and measure the resulting samples for amorphous fraction.
measurements: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) to compare glass transition and crystallization onsets
X-ray diffraction (XRD) for amorphous phase identification
Microscopic examination (TEM or SEM) to detect scale of any crystalline phases
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the boron-doped alloys do not exhibit a significantly increased critical thickness or if the supercooled liquid region and amorphous fraction remain unchanged, then the hypothesis is invalidated.
